items.title: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
items.snippet: Autonomous agents modify prompts, memories, tools, workflows, and policies using interaction histories. Yet a plausible modification is not necessarily suitable for persistent adoption: candidate selection is adaptive, evaluators may be imperfect, and local gains can hide degradation against an earlier baseline. We introduce Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of self-generated agent modifications. EGE separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified primary objective, protects declared capabilities through reference-relative non-inferiority tests,
items.title_ar: حوكمة قبول التحديثات الذاتية في وكلاء AI المستقلين
items.summary_ar: يقدم Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE)، إطاراً لحوكمة قبول التعديلات التي يولدها الـ agents لأنفسهم، مثل prompts وmemories وtools وpolicies. يفصل الإطار بين توليد المرشحين والتبني التأكيدي، ويقيّم المرشحين المجمدين على audits مزدوجة جديدة، ويشترط تحسناً ذا معنى في هدف أساسي محدد مسبقاً.
items.why_ar: يهم من يبني agents إنتاجية في البنك لأنه يحدد كيف تُعتمد تعديلات الـ agent بأمان دون تراجع خفي في الأداء.
items.title_en: Evidence-Governed Adoption of Self-Generated Updates in Autonomous AI Agents
items.summary_en: The paper proposes Evidence-Governed Evolution (EGE), a framework for governing adoption of agent-generated modifications to prompts, memories, tools, and policies. It separates candidate generation from confirmatory adoption, evaluates frozen candidates on fresh paired audits, and requires meaningful improvement on a prespecified objective while protecting declared capabilities through non-inferiority tests.
items.why_en: It matters to engineers deploying production agents, since it defines how agent self-modifications can be adopted safely without hidden regressions.

items.title: Mobile AI Factory: Building Specialized Language Models for Your Mobile Device
items.snippet: Small language models (SLMs) running on mobile devices can keep user data private and work without connectivity. But they perform well only when fine-tuned for the target task and sized for the target device, a process that today requires repeated expert tuning. We present {\it Mobile AI Factory}, an agentic system that builds a fine-tuned, quantized SLM for a given task and phone. Given a task specification and a target phone, an orchestrator LLM chooses whether to tune hyperparameters, mine real data, or generate synthetic examples, while fixed rules roll back changes that hurt accuracy. The factory searches from small to large models across base models and quantizations, adapts its accura
items.title_ar: Mobile AI Factory: بناء SLMs متخصصة للهاتف عبر agentic system
items.summary_ar: قدّم الباحثون Mobile AI Factory، وهو agentic system يبني SLM مع fine-tuning وquantization لمهمة محددة وهاتف مستهدف. يختار orchestrator LLM بين ضبط hyperparameters أو استخراج بيانات حقيقية أو توليد synthetic examples، وتتراجع قواعد ثابتة عن أي تغيير يخفض الدقة. يبحث النظام بين موديلات من الصغير إلى الكبير وخيارات quantization مختلفة.
items.why_ar: يهم مهندس الـ POCs لأنه يوضح كيف تُبنى نماذج on-device متخصصة بشكل آلي، وهو نمط قد يفيد حلول الخصوصية في التطبيقات المحمولة للبنك.
items.title_en: Mobile AI Factory builds task-specific SLMs for phones
items.summary_en: The authors present Mobile AI Factory, an agentic system that builds a fine-tuned, quantized SLM for a given task and phone. An orchestrator LLM chooses between tuning hyperparameters, mining real data, or generating synthetic examples, while fixed rules roll back accuracy-harming changes. The search spans small to large base models and quantization levels.
items.why_en: Useful for POC work on private on-device models, since it automates the fine-tuning and quantization loop for phone deployment.

items.title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System
items.snippet: Long-term memory lets LLM agents personalize, stay consistent, and reuse what worked before. Parametric memories need training, consolidation can lose details for good, and keeping every record leaves a growing store to search. We present MIRIX-2.0, a multi-agent memory system designed to be practical, accurate, and efficient at once. It is the most accurate of the compared systems on four of five QA benchmarks. It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, where it leads the strongest baseline by 14.3 points, and with AutoDream disabled it gains 31.0 and 22.0 points over HyperMem on single-hop and multi-hop document QA. As procedural memory, it yields the highest mean success among
items.title_ar: MIRIX-2.0: نظام memory متعدد الـ agents يتفوق على الأنظمة المقارنة
items.summary_ar: يقدّم MIRIX-2.0 نظام memory متعدد الـ agents للـ LLM agents، ويهدف إلى أن يكون عملياً ودقيقاً وفعالاً معاً. يحقق 91.4% على LoCoMo و72.6% على LongMemEval-S، ويتقدم على أقوى baseline بـ14.3 نقطة في أحد هذه الاختبارات. وعند تعطيل AutoDream يتفوق على HyperMem في document QA.
items.why_ar: يهم مهندس الـ agents لأن الذاكرة طويلة المدى تحدد جودة الـ personalization والاتساق في أنظمة البنك الحوارية.
items.title_en: MIRIX-2.0: a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents
items.summary_en: MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents aimed at being practical, accurate, and efficient. It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, leading the strongest baseline by 14.3 points on one of these benchmarks. With AutoDream disabled, it beats HyperMem on single-hop and multi-hop document QA.
items.why_en: Long-term agent memory directly affects personalization and consistency in conversational banking systems.

items.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands
items.snippet: With the rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs), an increasing number of users are turning to LLM-powered agents for conversational shopping in e-commerce. However, the user needs continue to change as new product categories, procurement scenarios, and feature requests emerge. At the same time, the product's execution harness-including its tools, skills, and operating procedures-continues to evolve to support increasingly sophisticated interactions. These changes create two practical challenges: 1) Demand drift alters the distribution, intent, and complexity of user requests, causing a model trained once to fall behind; 2) Harness evolution requires the model to use newly introduc
items.title_ar: G-CAST: تدريب ذاتي مستمر ومحكوم لـ agents التجارة الإلكترونية
items.summary_ar: تقترح الورقة إطار G-CAST لتدريب agents للتسوق الحواري في التجارة الإلكترونية بشكل ذاتي ومستمر. تعالج الورقة تغير طلبات المستخدمين وتطور الـ harness الذي يضم tools وskills وإجراءات التشغيل، والنص المتاح مقتطع ولا يذكر النتائج.
items.why_ar: يفيد في بناء agents تتكيف مع تغير متطلبات العملاء دون إعادة تدريب كاملة.
items.title_en: G-CAST: governed continual self-training for e-commerce agents
items.summary_en: The paper proposes G-CAST, a framework for continually self-training LLM agents used in conversational e-commerce shopping. It addresses demand drift and evolving harnesses that include tools, skills, and operating procedures. The available text is truncated and does not report results.
items.why_en: It is useful for building agents that adapt to changing customer demands without full retraining.

items.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
items.snippet: World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance. We show where dynamics lives in a frozen encoder: in a subspace shared across videos for predictive encoders such as V-JEPA, but not as a shared component of frame-wise,
items.title_ar: V-JEPA-LM: نماذج لغة مرئية تقرأ ديناميكيات الفيديو
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة V-JEPA-LM وهو video-language model يسعى لقراءة ديناميكيات الفيديو مثل الاتجاه والسرعة والترتيب بدلاً من استرجاع السمات النصية فقط. تبين الورقة أن مشفرات V-JEPA المجمدة تحمل معلومات حركية لا يستفيد منها الـ VLM، فمثلاً يقرأ linear probe السرعة بدقة 87% بينما تجيب النماذج اللغوية بمستوى عشوائي.
items.why_ar: يفيد المهندس في فهم حدود VLMs في التعامل مع الفيديو وطرق تحسينها.
items.title_en: V-JEPA-LM: video-language models that read dynamics beyond static representations
items.summary_en: The paper introduces V-JEPA-LM, a video-language model aimed at reading video dynamics such as direction, speed, and order rather than retrieving only text-aligned attributes. It shows that frozen V-JEPA encoders carry dynamics information the VLM fails to use, with a linear probe reading speed at 87% while the VLM answers at chance.
items.why_en: It helps this engineer understand the limits of current VLMs on video and how to improve them.

items.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
items.snippet: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input. We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training. Motivated by this observation, we propose MMFlas
items.title_ar: MMFlash: تسريع speculative decoding لنماذج الرؤية واللغة
items.summary_ar: تقدم الدراسة MMFlash لتسريع speculative decoding في النماذج متعددة الوسائط، عبر drafter يقترح كتلة tokens كاملة بتمرير أمامي واحد. تبين أن معدل القبول ينخفض من 46% في ربع الاعتماد البصري المنخفض إلى 22% في الربع الأعلى، وأن هذا الفرق يستمر بعد التدريب متعدد الوسائط.
items.why_ar: يهم من يبني أنظمة VLM ويحتاج تقليل inference latency في تطبيقات تجمع النص والصور.
items.title_en: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
items.summary_en: The paper introduces MMFlash to accelerate speculative decoding for multimodal models, using a diffusion drafter that proposes a full token block in one forward pass. It finds acceptance rates fall from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, and this gap persists after multimodal training.
items.why_en: It matters to engineers building vision-language systems who need lower inference latency.
